items.contrast: Whether the vine is being asked to become the trees’ king or is being invited for the vine’s own benefit.
items.reason: “For whose sake” asks about benefit or motive, so the vine is a plausible alternative and the window does not directly state whose benefit is intended. A bounded rewrite such as “Whose king did the trees ask the vine to be?” makes the key uniquely the trees, as shown by “our king.” The underlying possessive relation is a concrete distinction rather than mere word lookup.
